pr_title: Pad GPG Key ID with preceding zeroes
pr_body:
The go crypto library does not pad keyIDs to 16 characters with preceding zeroes. This
is a somewhat confusing thing for most users who expect these to have preceding zeroes.

This PR prefixes any sub 16 length KeyID with preceding zeroes and removes preceding
zeroes from KeyIDs inputted on the API.

Fix #20876

Signed-off-by: Andrew Thornton <art27@cantab.net>

issue_context.title: Mirrored commits omitting leading zero from GPG Key ID
issue_context.body:
### Description

I am mirroring my public GitHub repo into Gitea.

Commits mirrored into Gitea are missing the leading zero from the GPG Key ID, resulting in a `No known key found for this signature in database` message.

- GPG key ID: 0EC57C6D1392E54F
- [GitHub commit](https://github.com/calvinbui/ansible-monorepo/commit/18bfcad45ede0fbd88f165e4baa378cf0d01dd35) showing `0EC57C6D1392E54F`
- [Gitea demo site mirrored commit](https://try.gitea.io/calvinbui/ansible-monorepo/commit/18bfcad45ede0fbd88f165e4baa378cf0d01dd35) showing `EC57C6D1392E54F`

### Gitea Version

1.17.0

### Can you reproduce the bug on the Gitea demo site?

Yes

review_comments:
Can keys start with zeros, or is a leading zero always seen as padding?
Because if it is the former, this will probably produce a lot of problems in the future…

Take a look at pubkey.KeyIDString()

The trimming is to fix potential issues relating to that
